purpose: Concept reference only; Task007 overrides spatial invention

concepts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: game environment concept reference for an optimized Roblox museum kit, not a final screenshot or a new floor plan.
Style: visibly low-poly to mid-low-poly 3D game art with broad flat colour regions, clean silhouettes, deliberately simplified 8-to-12-sided curved objects, plain satin materials and economical geometry. Premium through composition and proportion, never through dense detail. It must look achievable with a small reusable modular asset kit.
Coordinated palette: warm ivory stone, mushroom-grey dado, charcoal exhibition bases, muted aged-brass rim accents, deep museum teal, pale desaturated blue display glazing, small amber security indicator strips, restrained oxblood restricted-room accents. Reuse exactly these material families throughout.
Architecture: Victoria-inspired classical Kolkata museum character; broad columns, simple rounded arches, shallow trim bands and generous ceiling height. The existing historic shell stays the main architecture. No new staircase, balcony, storey, exterior, doorway or changed room arrangement.
Lighting: warm diffuse daylight with soft clean shadows, readable midtones, a small warm exhibit emphasis and restrained cool glazing. No dramatic darkness, volumetric effects, mirror floors, realistic reflection or cinematic lens tricks.
Production constraints: every display reads as a few simple mesh pieces; transparent glass is restrained and clear, cases have thin plain frames; exhibit content is fictional and stylized, no claim of real museum possessions. Keep all walkways wide and uncluttered. No people, realistic human figures, crowds, active laser beams, smoke, HUD, logos, small unreadable labels, intricate carvings, dense friezes, decorative clutter, photorealism, textures or hyper-detail. No new obstacles in walking lanes. Landscape room view.

Primary request: the main orientation space of the approved Victoria Memorial museum robbery. Camera: standing player eye height about 6 studs above the floor, a broad 26 mm-equivalent view from one axial entry, with level verticals and clear view across the hall. Foreground: open pale floor with one restrained deep-teal wayfinding plaque at the side, no exhibit or barrier across the entrance. Midground: the existing simple pale central memorial figure on its small original plinth, a broad dark radial floor ring around it, generous space to walk around both sides; no new loot exhibit here. Background: preserved tall simple arcade and opposite axial opening; suggest the soft blue inner dome above through broad surfaces. Four onward routes must remain visually legible. One slim museum information stand can sit beside an existing pier, never in the main axis. Preserve the grand historic shell in the supporting screenshot; remove debug labels and coloured greybox blocks in the interpretation. Focus on quiet orientation, generous negative space and simple heritage proportions.

Primary request: welcoming public exhibition gallery, approximately 33 by 34 studs, four easy exhibits, matching the supporting greybox composition. Camera: eye level just inside the vestibule connection, angled gently across the room toward the existing paired openings in the new partition. Foreground: a compact four-stud-square document display at one side and a small decorative miniature on the other side, both leaving the central lane open. Midground: two other compact exhibits at the opposite outer corners, including one simply framed fictional river study on a freestanding support within its original pedestal footprint. Background: two simple ten-stud-wide partition doorways into the smaller collections room; retain the existing courtyard connection off the side. No extra paintings or new cases elsewhere. Use four separate compact objects with clear silhouettes, plain teal information plaques and modest brass rim details. The reusable case family should have a charcoal plinth, ivory shallow top and almost-clear pale blue glazing. Architecture stays light and airy with a plain barrel vault and existing classical columns. This room should feel safe, approachable and easy to read.

Primary request: medium-risk painting gallery in an existing long wing, about 57 by 34 studs, with four exhibit positions and two independent connections. Camera: eye-level three-quarter view from one end looking lengthwise; use the supporting gallery screenshot only as the approved architectural language, not as a different floor plan. Foreground: one small framed fictional monsoon street study on a compact freestanding painting display within a four-stud-square support footprint, kept beside the perimeter. Midground: two widely separated displays showing simple flat-colour geometric river/city/garden artwork, restrained rectangular brass frames and charcoal backs; show the open broad central circulation strip clearly. Background: a fourth portfolio display near the opposite side, one existing vestibule opening and the side courtyard connection, both visibly unobstructed. Keep all painting images original, simplified masses with perhaps a boat shape or a tree silhouette, no realistic photographs and no tiny detail. Frames and dado trims are reused, not elaborate unique sculpture. Warm ivory, muted brass and deep teal, slightly richer focal displays than the public gallery, same low-poly game-art language.

Primary request: medium-risk sculpture gallery inside an existing 57 by 34-stud wing with exactly three separate exhibit positions. Camera: low enough to feel like a Roblox player, around six studs above floor, diagonal view with a level horizon. Foreground: a short square charcoal-and-ivory pedestal carrying a simple abstract bronze made from two broad interlocking faceted shapes, set to one side. Midground: a fictional ceremonial vessel with an eight- or ten-sided body and two thick simple handles, seated in a compact medium display unit near the perimeter; show generous unoccupied walking space around it. Background: the third small decorative sculpture/collection display, the existing tall simple vault rhythm and unobstructed side courtyard opening. Maintain the approved wing's two route connections; do not add a central island blocking the route. Reuse the same plinths, brass case rails, plain museum plaques and shallow wall trims as the other concepts. A sculptural silhouette may be interesting, but surfaces must stay extremely simple. No realistic human statues, carved relief, heaps of objects or ornate metal filigree.

Primary request: optional high-security exhibition in the approved compact 36 by 34-stud room. Camera: player eye-height view from the vestibule edge looking toward the paired archive doorways, using the supporting screenshot as the spatial arrangement. Foreground: one discreet static-laser emitter pair marks a side branch; the visible objects are slim charcoal housings with amber lens slots, no active beams. Midground: retain the small central eight-by-eight-stud flush electrical-floor reservation, made of a few broad charcoal inlay panels and an amber edge border, with readable walking space around both sides. A moving-laser housing stays on the other side's reserved pad. Background: precisely two protected exhibit cases near the rear perimeter, one with a fictional angular jewelled insignia and one rare ceremonial object, each within its six-stud case footprint; behind them the existing two simple ten-stud archive openings remain visible. One compact terminal is parked beside the entry-side wall. Cases are premium through stronger charcoal bases and muted brass corner rails, not through extra ornament. No additional loot, doors or devices. Restrained oxblood threshold band, clear path hierarchy, clean inactive equipment, same historic architecture and low-poly palette.

Primary request: the approved restricted archive, a compact 19 by 34-stud outer-wing room, functional and quieter than the galleries. Camera: eye-height from one of its two partition doorways, diagonal view across the central display island toward the other open return path. Foreground: keep a broad clear lane by the doorway, with a slim charcoal terminal off the side and one plain inactive laser housing, all confined to their existing reservations. Midground: exactly two compact freestanding displays sit along the central island, one protected rare folio and one fictional ceremonial collection; leave a clear loop around both ends. A single shallow closed secure archive cabinet may sit against the far wall as a future dressing option, never projecting into a doorway or walking lane. Background: plain ivory-and-grey wall treatment, modest classical vault inherited from the shell, a simple existing window and the second return doorway. Archive identity comes from broad labelled-drawer-like colour blocks without readable tiny text, a dark teal cabinet body and restrained brass pulls. No dense book stacks, no desks filling the room, no new storage maze, no realistic manuscripts. Simple folded folio shapes and a few broad artefact silhouettes only. Maintain the same visibly low-poly game art as the other five references.
